questions.question: Which of the following is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Mitochondria**__ is known as the powerhouse of the cell.
 
• They are called so since they are responsible for cellular respiration or energy release from food.
 
• The endoplasmic reticulum is a membrane system that functions as a packaging and manufacturing system.
 
• The nucleus is an organelle which contains DNA of eukaryotic organisms.
 
• The cytoplasm is enclosed by a cell membrane and is a thick fluid which fills each cell.

questions.question: ________ is the smallest bone in the human body.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Stapes__**.

 
• **Smallest Bone in the Human Body**

 
 
• At 3 mm x 2.5 mm, the "**stapes**" in the middle ear is the smallest named bone in the human body.
 
• The shape of a stirrup, this bone is one of three in the middle ear, collectively known as the ossicles.
 
• The ossicles convey sound pressure waves from the outer ear (and eardrum) to the inner ear, where the waves are translated into nerve impulses that go to the brain for identification.
 
• The other two ossicles are the malleus (hammer) and the incus (anvil).

questions.question: The ______ in the human body controls every activity that you perform.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The **nervous system__ **in the human body controls every activity that you perform.
 
• It consists of two parts the central nervous system and the peripheral nervous system.
 
 
• Central nervous system: Brain and Spinal Cord
 
• Peripheral nervous system: Cranial nerves, spinal nerves and sensory organs
 
 
 
• The nervous system uses nerves to communicate between organs of the body and the brain/spinal cord.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles is known as suicide bag?
questions.solution:
__**Lysosomes cell organelles are known as suicide bags.**__

**Lysosomes:**

 
• Lysosomes are tiny spherical sac-like structures evenly distributed in the cytoplasm.
 
• These vesicular structures contain destructive enzymes called hydrolases.
 
• The hydrolases enzyme is capable of breaking down a wide variety of food particles so the chief function of the lysosome is digestion.

**Mitochondria:**

 
• Mitochondria are **tiny bodies of varying shapes and sizes.**
 
• Mitochondria **contain their own DNA.**
 
• It is the site of cellular respiration.
 
• Oxidation releases energy, a portion of which is used to form ATP (Adenosine triphosphate).
 
• Mitochondria synthesize the energy-rich compound ATP so they are also known as the **‘powerhouse of the cell’.**

**Golgi apparatus:**

 
• Golgi apparatus or Golgi bodies or Golgi complex arises from the membrane of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum, which in turn have originated from the rough endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• The synthetic products of the cell i.e. proteins, hormones, and enzymes that are collected by the Golgi vacuoles and secreted into the cytoplasm.

**Endoplasmic Reticulum**

 
• On the one end, it's connected to the outer membrane of the nucleus and on the other end to the plasma membrane.
 
• It forms the supporting skeletal framework of the cell.
 
• It** provides a pathway for the distribution of nuclear material from one cell to another.**
 
• It provides an increased surface for various enzymatic reactions.

questions.question: Which part of the body is responsible for the manufacture of red blood cells?
questions.solution:
Option **2 **is the correct answer:__ Red Blood Cells are produced in **Bone Marrow**__.

**Bone Marrow:**

 
• Bone Marrow is the soft tissue present inside the **Medullary cavities of a bone**.
 
• It is mainly present in the hip and thigh bones.
 
• Bone marrow** produces immature cells called Stem cells** that can transform into various kinds of cells later on.
 
• **Mesenchymal and Hematopoietic** are the two types of stem cells produced by Bone Marrow.
 
• Mesenchymal transform into fat cartilage and bones whereas Hematopoietic turn into Blood cells (RBC, WBC and Platelets).

**Red Blood Cells (RBC)**:

 
• **​**These are also known as **Erythrocytes**.
 
• These disc-shaped cells contain **Haemoglobin** and have **no nucleus**.
 
• RBCs are produced in Bone Marrow and Spleen & Liver (in the foetus).
 
• The average lifetime of RBCs is **120 days**.
 
• RBCs, when produced in more amount, leads to **Polycythemia **and if produced in lesser amount leads to **Anaemia**.

questions.question: The normal temperature of the human body is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ​37°C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The normal temperature** of the** human body** is typically around **98.6 degrees Fahrenheit or 37 degrees Celsius.**
 
• However, it's important to note that individual body temperatures can **vary slightly**, and factors such as time of day, physical activity, and overall health can influence body temperature.

• The human body is composed of several systems that work together to maintain its functions and overall well-being. Here are some key systems of the human body:
 
 
• **Circulatory System**:
 
• This system consists of the heart, blood vessels, and blood.
 
• **Respiratory System**:
 
• Comprised of the lungs and airways, the respiratory system facilitates the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide.
 
• **Digestive System:**
 
• The digestive system includes organs such as the mouth, esophagus, stomach, intestines, liver, and pancreas. 
 
• **Nervous System:**
 
• The nervous system consists of the brain, spinal cord, and nerves.
 
• **Muscular System:**
 
• Comprising muscles throughout the body, the muscular system enables movement, maintains posture, generates heat, and supports various bodily functions.
 
• **Skeletal System: **
 
• The skeletal system consists of bones, cartilage, ligaments, and tendons. 
 
• **Endocrine System**:
 
• This system includes glands such as the pituitary, thyroid, adrenal, and reproductive glands. 
 
• **Immune System:**
 
• The immune system defends the body against infections, diseases, and foreign substances.
 
• **Urinary System:**
 
• The urinary system comprises the kidneys, bladder, ureters, and urethra.
 
• **Reproductive System: **
 
• The reproductive system is responsible for the production of offspring.

questions.question: Which acid is produced in the human stomach to help with the digestion of food?
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• The stomach is a muscular hollow organ.
 
• It takes in food from the esophagus (gullet or food pipe), mixes it, breaks it down, and then passes it on to the small intestine in small portions.
 
• The stomach stores the food for 4-5 hours.
 
• The food mixes thoroughly with the acidic gastric juice of the stomach by the churning movements of its muscular wall and is called the chyme. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__

• It functions by destroying harmful microorganisms present in the food particles.
 
 
 
• The digestive system of the human body comprises a group of organs that work together in converting food into energy and other basic nutrients to power the body. 
 
• The stomach serves as a muscular bag that is situated towards the left side of the abdominal cavity, beneath the diaphragm.
 
 
• This vital organ acts as a storage for food and provides enough time to digest meals.
 
• The stomach also produces digestive enzymes and hydrochloric acid that maintains the process of digestion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

• Digestion is necessary for breaking down food particles into nutrients that are used by the body as an energy source, cell repair, and growth.
 
• Food and drink need to be converted into smaller molecules of nutrients before it is absorbed by the blood and carried to the cells throughout the body.
 
• The body breaks the nutrients present in the drinks and food into carbohydrates, vitamins, fats, and proteins.

questions.question: In humans, each cell normally contains _________ pairs of chromosomes.
questions.solution:
​In humans, each cell normally contains __**23**__** pairs** of **chromosomes**.

 
• In humans, each cell normally contains** 23 pairs of chromosomes**, for a total of **46**.
 
• **Twenty-two** of these pairs, called autosomes, look the same in both** males and females**.
 
• The **23rd pair**, the **sex chromosomes**, differ between males and females.
 
• Females have** two copies of the X chromosome**, while **males **have **one X and one Y chromosome**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the universal recipient blood group?
questions.solution:
• **The AB blood group** is the universal recipient blood group.
 
• The blood group of a person is inherited and the blood group depends on the type of antigens on the surface of the red blood cells (RBCs) of the body.
 
• There are two types of antigens, type A and type B which create 4 blood groups, A, B, AB and O.
 
• Since people with blood group AB have both antigens on the surface of the RBCs they can accept any type.
 
• On the other hand blood group O is a universal donor as they have none of the antigens on the surface of the RBCs.

questions.question: Within what pH range does the human body work?
questions.solution:
**The pH value **of** Human body** is __**7.0 to 7.8.**__

 
• **pH scale** used to measure that the water based solution is acidic or basic.
 
• **Pure water is neither acidic nor basic at room temperature** (25 ° C or 77 ° F) and has a** pH value of 7.**

questions.question: Which of the following terms is used to describe the outside layer of skin on the human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Epidermis.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The epidermis is the **outermost layer of skin on the body.**
 
• It protects our body from harm, keeps your body hydrated, produces new skin cells, and contains melanin, which determines the color of your skin.
 
• Our skin has** 3 main layers and the outermost layer in our body.**
 
• The** other two layers of skin are the dermis and hypoderms.**
 
• The epidermis is the thinnest layer of skin, but it's responsible for protecting you from the outside world, and it's composed of five layers of its own.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It can also be found in your internal organs and glands.
 
• It is a protective protein, less prone to scratching or tearing than other types of cells your body produces.
 
 
 
• **Larynx:**
 
 
• It is part of the respiratory system.
 
• It contains vocal cords and is essential to human speech, so it's often called the voice box.
 
 
 
• **Quadriceps:**

• Cell types used are epithelial cells, endothelial cells, muscle cells, schwannoma, and hepatocytes.
 
 
 
• **Collagen** is the most abundant protein in mammals.
 
 
• In cell culture, it is used to study the growth, differentiation, and migration of cells. 
 
• Collagen Type I is used for fibroblasts or endothelial cells.
 
• Collagen Type II may be used for Chondrocytes and epithelial cells.
 
 
 
• 
 **Fibronectin** is a multifunctional protein involved in cell adhesion and spreading.

 
 
• 
 It also regulates cellular morphology, cell migration, cytoskeletal organization, hemostasis, and wound repair.
 
 
• 
 For cell types such as epithelial cells, mesenchymal cells, neuronal cells, fibroblasts cells, and endothelial cells you may use fibronectin.

questions.question: Epilepsy is a disorder that affects which of the following parts of the human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brain cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Epilepsy is a neurological disorder primarily affecting the **brain cells**.
 
• It is characterized by recurrent, unprovoked seizures due to abnormal electrical activity in the brain.
 
• Seizures can vary from brief and nearly undetectable to long periods of vigorous shaking.
 
• Epilepsy can be caused by various factors including genetics, brain injury, or other underlying health conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seizure Types:**

 
 
• Seizures are broadly classified into two categories: focal (partial) seizures and generalized seizures.
 
• Focal seizures originate from one area of the brain, while generalized seizures affect both hemispheres.
 
 
 
• **Diagnosis:**
 
 
• Diagnosis typically involves neurological exams, EEG (electroencephalogram), and imaging tests like MRI or CT scans.
 
• These tests help identify the underlying cause and the type of epilepsy.
 
 
 
• **Treatment:**
 
 
• Treatment options include anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs), lifestyle changes, surgery, or neurostimulation devices.
 
• The choice of treatment depends on the type of seizures, their frequency, and the individual's overall health.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Life:**
 
 
• Epilepsy can significantly impact daily life, affecting education, employment, and social interactions.
 
• Proper management and support can help individuals lead fulfilling lives despite the condition.

questions.question: The levels of glycated hemoglobin in blood are influenced by many factors. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

• Hence, glycated haemoglobin is the haemoglobin which has a sugar (generally glucose) attached to it.
 
• **HbA1C test** is a popular test to **detect diabetes** as glyacted haemoglobin is easiest to detect.
 
• Higher amount of HbA1C indicates higher level of blood sugar levels, leading to diabetes.

• Blood loss, blood transfusion, anaemia, Iron deficiency, Pregnancy, high dose of Vitamin C etc.
